verdict.rationale: Community threads show a vulnerability-response process for the Bluetooth Titan key flaw: a described security issue (comm-9), an 'Update on your Titan Security Key' email to owners, and free replacements (comm-12). The fix reached users by physically replacing keys, not by firmware updates, and the replacement flow required a support chat, an RMA and a card payment (comm-10, comm-11). Affected-key identification also looked weak, since Google could not tell a Feitian MultiPass apart from its own key (comm-12). missing for 10: first-party security advisories in the evidence, a documented affected-model lookup, any field firmware-update mechanism or documentation, and a documented vulnerability-disclosure policy.
